correctness.rationale: The finite-time F_s evolution equation is exact for bounded-by-time clocks; its regular Kummer solution is verified by initial conditions and exact power series. For s<1 the Kummer asymptotic gives Lambda(s)=s/(1-s), and no-reset events plus monotonicity establish infinite Lambda for s>=1. Lambda is essentially smooth, lsc, and exponentially tight; the Gärtner–Ellis theorem yields a full annealed LDP with I(y)=(sqrt(y)-1)^2. Differentiation and analytic uniformity at s=0 give the exact mean, variance constant, and CLT. The CHECK.py test (561 checks) corroborates the algebra and probabilistic construction; finite checks are not used as proofs.

originality.rationale: The full annealed LDP of the operational clock at logarithmic speed, with its explicit rate (sqrt(y)-1)^2, is not among the source results: arXiv:2608.02297v1 supplies the exact Kummer factor and typical log scale, whereas arXiv:2105.02633v3 proves a general quenched LDP and explicitly identifies the annealed upper bound as beyond that theorem (Remark 1.5). The Gaussian and exact-moment formulas are quantitative companions rather than an asserted general priority. The result is a derived special-case theorem, not a new generating function. Direct literature, indexed-finding and own-ledger searches did not identify an earlier statement of this annealed clock rate; these searches cannot certify uniqueness.
